newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: COSTELLO CHALLENGES BANKS TO FOLLOW COMMONWEALTH CUT
Federal Treasurer, Peter Costello, says the Commonwealth Bank's move to cut its home loan rates is great news for home buyers.
The bank has cut its standard home loan rate to 7.5 percent.
Mr Costello says the point-seven-of-one per cent cut takes rates to their lowest point since June 1974.
He's challenged other banks to follow the Commonwealth's lead.
Mr Costello says standard variable home loan rates have now fallen by 2.95 per cent since last March.
WOODS' AGREEMENT "IMPLIES NO GUILT"
Liberal Senator, Bob Woods, is continuing to maintain his innocence, after an application for an apprehended violence order against him was dropped today.
Roxanne Cameron, a former lover of Senator Woods, applied for a restraining order on the same day last week that Senator Woods tendered his resignation from Federal Parliament.
North Sydney Local Court heard both Senator Woods and 30-year-old Ms Cameron had reached a mutual agreement to stay away from one another, and from one another's families.
But Senator Woods' solicitor, Phillip Gibson, says the striking of the deal in no way implies guilt on the part of his client.
Mr Gibson says the agreement puts an end to the matter.
ANTHRAX FOUND ON THREE MORE PROPERTIES
Another three properties in Victoria's Goulburn Valley have now been confirmed as having dairy herds infected with Anthrax, bringing the total to 34.
The three were confirmed this afternoon, after an earlier confirmation that another cow had died from the disease on a property where Anthrax had already been found.
There are now 72 confirmed cattle deaths due to Anthrax and a total of 96 dairy herds had been quarantined for vaccination. - - - -
NTH QLD CYCLONE NO LONGER A CYCLONE
The cyclone which had been heading towards the North Queensland coast has weakened into a tropical low.
The weather bureau says the remains of Tropical Cyclone Gillian are centred about 70 kilometres north-north-east of Townsville.
Bureau forecaster, Darryl Thom, says heavy rain is expected to continue between Ayr and Mackay, and strong winds will affect the coast from Lucinda south to Bowen.
Further advice will be issued at four PM, local time.
QLD PREMIER PREFERS THREATS, SAYS FORMER ATSIC HEAD
Former Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission head Lois O'Donoghue says Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge seems to prefer to make threats rather than admit his government's mistakes.
She says the Queensland Government has to deal with the consequences of ignoring the Native Title Act when handing out leases.
Miss O'Donoghue says Mr Borbidge's attitude towards Aborigines will ensure reconciliation is made more difficult.
Miss O'Donoghue says she was disturbed to hear Mr Borbidge say unless native title is extinguished Australia can forget about reconciliation.
NSW POLICE TO REGAIN RIGHT TO APPEAL IF SACKED
The New South Wales Government's commitment to restore a right of industrial appeal for sacked police officers has been welcomed by the state's Labour Council.
Police Minister, Paul Whelan, announced yesterday a working party would be established to draw up a streamlined appeals process within the industrial courts system.
The government had faced a strong campaign for the restoration of a right of industrial appeal since it scrapped access to the commission for police late last year.
Labour Council Secretary, Peter Sams, says the new system should be an improvement.
